_note: Rhode Island habitability rule, retrieved verbatim from the R.I. Legislature statute server (webserver.rilegislature.gov) on 2026-06-20, Title 34 Ch. 18 (Residential Landlord and Tenant Act). § 34-18-22(a)(2) makes it a mandatory landlord duty to make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition; § 34-18-22(a)(1) requires compliance with building and housing codes affecting health and safety. § 34-18-17(a)(1) separately bars any rental-agreement provision by which the tenant waives or foregoes rights or remedies under the chapter, and § 34-18-17(b) makes such a provision unenforceable. Together these make an 'as-is' / habitability-waiver clause unenforceable in RI. status=draft-unverified: must be reviewed by a Rhode Island tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: "As-is" / waiver of the landlord's duty to keep the premises habitable
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-22(a), the landlord must comply with health-and-safety building/housing codes and make all repairs necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition — a non-discretionary statutory duty. Because § 34-18-17(a)(1) bars (and § 34-18-17(b) makes unenforceable) any clause by which the tenant waives rights or remedies under the chapter, an 'as-is' clause or a waiver of the landlord's repair/habitability duty does not hold up.
rules.tenant_explainer: You can't sign away your right to a livable home. Rhode Island makes it the landlord's job to keep the place up to code and in fit, habitable condition — so 'tenant accepts the unit as-is' or 'landlord has no duty to repair' clauses don't hold up.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-22(a)(1)-(2)
citations.quote: A landlord shall: (1) Comply with the requirements of applicable building and housing codes affecting health and safety; (2) Make all repairs and do whatever is necessary to put and keep the premises in a fit and habitable condition;

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-17(a)(1)
citations.quote: A rental agreement may not provide that the tenant: (1) Agrees to waive or forego rights or remedies under this chapter;
